overview: The two lobes of the pituitary gland, differing in whether they manufacture their own hormones or just release ones made elsewhere.
genZNote: Anterior pituitary: its own hormone factory. Posterior pituitary: just a storage and release dock for hormones made in the hypothalamus.

aspects.label: Hormone Origin
aspects.valueA: Synthesises its own hormones (e.g. GH, TSH, FSH, LH, prolactin, ACTH).
aspects.valueB: Stores and releases hormones made by the hypothalamus (oxytocin, ADH) — does not synthesise them itself.

aspects.label: Tissue Type
aspects.valueB: Neural tissue, an extension of the hypothalamus.

aspects.label: Control Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Regulated by hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones via a portal blood system.
aspects.valueB: Regulated by direct nerve impulses from the hypothalamus.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Oxytocin and ADH are made in the hypothalamus but released from the posterior pituitary — a classic exam trap about where a hormone is 'made' versus 'released'.
overlay.memoryTrick: Anterior = actually makes its own hormones. Posterior = just passes along the hypothalamus's hormones.
overlay.commonMisconception: The posterior pituitary is often wrongly credited with producing ADH and oxytocin — production happens in the hypothalamus; the posterior pituitary only stores and releases them.
